purpose: A feature-level parity contract across source discovery, Payload schema, editor experience, frontend runtime, migration, and verification. It complements the 297-route inventory; it does not replace or redefine route ownership.

authority.sourceBaseline: The live public Trayport site and the equivalent desktop-local WordPress deployment

statusDefinitions.complete: All six dimensions are satisfied for the feature's stated boundary; this does not widen that boundary or imply launch readiness.
statusDefinitions.partial: Useful target behavior exists, but one or more required dimensions remain incomplete.
statusDefinitions.missing: A required target capability is absent in at least one dimension.
statusDefinitions.deferred: The requirement is accepted but intentionally scheduled for a later delivery slice.
statusDefinitions.excluded: The feature has an explicit approved omission or replacement disposition.
statusDefinitions.decision: Source behavior or target ownership is ambiguous and requires a recorded product decision before implementation can close.

features.title: Production route corpus
features.targetOwner: Payload route owners, redirects, and two derived indexes
features.boundary: The approved 297 canonical public route owners, distinct from dependencies, aliases, and navigation occurrences.

source.summary: The reproducible inventory proves 297 unique included route owners with zero unknown archetypes, including the EEX News Page reached from the active published banner.

schema.summary: All approved route-owner families and route invariants have target models.

editor.summary: The accepted models are editable, but the complete production population and review queues are not present.

runtime.summary: Thirty-one Payload documents, one redirect owner, and two virtual indexes are accepted; 263 owners remain plan-only.

migration.summary: The deterministic target plan covers all owners, while the accepted load remains a 34-owner runtime slice.

verification.summary: Source-scope verification passes; complete imported, rendered, linked, and reviewed route acceptance does not.

acceptance: All 297 owners load without unresolved relationships or duplicate canonical paths.
Every listing-linked detail renders complete content and passes route, link, media, SEO, and visual review.
features.nextAction: Extend the immutable import and acceptance review from 34 to all 297 route owners.

features.title: Page and article block composition
features.targetOwner: Payload Pages, Articles, and the bounded Trayport block library
features.boundary: Authoritative WordPress flexible-content semantics mapped to typed, reusable Payload blocks and section structure.

source.summary: Observed layouts and authoritative field families have explicit dispositions.

schema.summary: The accepted top-level and section-component catalogue is modeled with bounded controls.

editor.summary: Editors have visual section presets, meaningful summaries, collapsible groups, and advanced controls separated from primary tasks.

runtime.summary: Configured accepted blocks have typed renderer ownership and responsive section composition.

migration.summary: Accepted roots transform deterministically, but the full production corpus has not been loaded and remediated.

verification.summary: Schema-renderer totality and accepted-route tests pass; production-wide visual and editorial review remains open.

acceptance: Every in-scope source layout maps explicitly with no silent drops.
Every visible editor control has tested runtime behavior across the production corpus.
features.nextAction: Run the full-corpus transform and control-to-runtime audit, then review exceptions with editors.

features.title: Navigation and footer
features.targetOwner: Payload Navigation, Footer, and Site Settings globals
features.boundary: Active ACF dropdown/footer configuration, shared utility actions, legal copy, social destinations, and managed internal links.

source.summary: The active ACF options are authoritative; classic WordPress menus are excluded.

schema.summary: Navigation, footer, social, notice, and managed-link data have bounded global models.

editor.summary: Shared configuration is editable independently of route documents.

runtime.summary: The accepted internal roots work; 34 plan-only same-site destinations intentionally fall back to the live site.

migration.summary: The accepted ACF globals and link dispositions import deterministically.

verification.summary: Desktop/mobile interaction tests pass, while all destinations cannot become internal until their owners are accepted.

acceptance: All launch navigation and footer destinations resolve to accepted internal owners or approved external destinations.
Desktop, mobile, keyboard, focus, and current-location behavior passes.
features.nextAction: Convert each live-site fallback to a managed internal link as its route owner is accepted.

features.title: Scheduled and targeted page banners
features.targetOwner: Payload Banners collection and page banner runtime
features.boundary: Reusable small/large banners targeting all or selected pages, with start/end dates, first/second/last placement, priority, managed media/link, and lifecycle notifications.

source.summary: The banner CPT, ACF fields, active-window resolver, placement behavior, and four notification moments are identified.

schema.summary: Payload models content, layout, active dates, page targeting, placement, priority, and private CMS recipients; a non-versioned delivery ledger owns operational notification state.

editor.summary: Editors and administrators can draft, schedule, target, order, and publish banners through bounded fields; a saved banner can be previewed on a target Page outside its public date window.

runtime.summary: Request-time active filtering, first/second/last page slots, and a retry-bounded four-event notification task with an exact-schedule delivery ledger exist; production SMTP and scheduler execution are not yet accepted, and SMTP cannot make the final send/ledger transition exactly-once.

migration.summary: Extractor, relationship transform, recipient-review state, load priority, and database migrations exist; the live source run contains four banners plus all five dependent Pages and referenced media.

verification.summary: Date, targeting, grouping, presentation, transform, notification, source-load, and desktop/mobile browser acceptance pass; production SMTP/scheduler evidence remains open.

acceptance: A banner can target every page or selected Pages and appears only inside its inclusive start/end window.
First, second, and last placements and small/large presentations match or explicitly improve the live behavior.
Existing active/future banner data and relationships import idempotently.
Configured recipients receive deduplicated before-live, live, before-offline, and offline notifications.
features.nextAction: Complete production scheduler/SMTP recipient acceptance, including the migrated-recipient review workflow and monitoring for the rare stale-lease duplicate window after SMTP acceptance.

A production-like test submission reaches an approved HubSpot destination without bypassing consent.
